questions.q: You want training jobs to cost nothing while no job is running, but to scale up automatically when one is submitted. Which setup fits?
options: A compute instance that you leave running
A compute cluster with min_instances set to 0
A curated environment
A Key Vault with a schedule
questions.explain: A compute cluster autoscales between min_instances and max_instances; with a minimum of zero, no nodes run (or bill for compute) while idle.

questions.q: What is a compute instance in Azure Machine Learning?
options: A shared pool of nodes used only for batch scoring
A Docker image cached in the container registry
A managed cloud workstation for one person, with Jupyter, JupyterLab and VS Code
A dataset stored in the default datastore
questions.explain: A compute instance is a managed cloud-based workstation for a data scientist with a single owner. It bills while running, so idle shutdown is important.

questions.q: What does serverless compute mean when you submit a training job?
options: You omit the compute name and the service provisions capacity for the job, so there is no cluster for you to create
The job runs on your laptop instead of the cloud
The job cannot use an environment
You must create a compute instance first
questions.explain: Per the Microsoft docs, you don't need to create serverless compute; leaving out the compute setting on a command job uses it.

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the three environment categories described in the lesson?
options: Curated
System-managed (conda spec on a base image)
User-managed (your own image or build context)
Compute-managed (chosen automatically from the VM size)
questions.explain: Environments are curated, system-managed or user-managed. They are defined by packages and images, not derived from the VM size.

questions.q: Why does the lesson pin exact package versions in the conda spec?
options: Conda refuses to install unpinned packages
Pinned specs make jobs run faster on GPUs
Azure charges less for pinned environments
A changed version makes a different environment, so pinning keeps runs reproducible across machines and time
questions.explain: The demo shows one changed pin producing a different hash. Unpinned dependencies drift, which is how 'it worked on my machine' happens in the cloud.
